title: Maximum Star Sum of a Graph
summary: Given an undirected graph with nodes numbered 0 to n-1, and a value array for each node, find the maximum star sum of a subgraph containing at most k edges.
statement: Given an undirected graph with nodes numbered 0 to n-1, and a value array for each node, find the maximum star sum of a subgraph containing at most k edges. A star graph has a center node with zero or more neighbors. The star sum is the total value of nodes in the star graph.
constraints: Choose any center node and at most k of its direct neighbors.
The star sum is the center value plus chosen neighbor values.
Return the maximum star sum; choosing zero neighbors is allowed.
hints: Negative neighbors can never improve a star because selecting fewer than k is allowed.
Collect positive neighbor values for every possible center.
Sort each center’s values descending and add its largest k to the center value.
For a fixed center, the positive top-k choice is optimal; checking every center yields the global maximum.
editorial: For a fixed center, the positive top-k choice is optimal; checking every center yields the global maximum.

tests.explanation: Center 3 has value four; choosing neighbors valued ten and two gives the maximum star sum sixteen.
All neighbor additions are negative, so choose center value -2 with no edges in the star.
